title: Reduced tensor with an algebraic closure detects separability of a finite field extension
statement: Let k be a field, let K/k be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let kbar be an algebraic closure of k [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. If K tensor_k kbar is reduced (has no nonzero nilpotent elements), then K/k is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions), implication (4) => (1), together with Tag 030V (algebra-lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension)

proof.text: Assume for contradiction that $K/k$ is not separable. By [lem-pc-finite-inseparable-element], there is an element $\alpha\in K$ whose minimal polynomial over $k$ is inseparable.
The hypothesis of [lem-pc-inseparable-tensor-nilpotent] is now satisfied, so $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$ contains a nonzero nilpotent element and is not reduced.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 030V (algebra-lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension), together with Tag 030W

proof.text: This contradicts the assumed reducedness of $K\otimes_k\bar{k}$. Hence the assumption was false and $K/k$ is separable.
